routes.description: Establish that the principal immaterial, ordered, rational, informational, moral, and purposive features of reality require an adequate grounding cause, and that their cumulative implications identify a transcendent personal creator more completely than materialist atheism does.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant features of reality are shown to require foundations unavailable to materialist atheism, the proposed theistic ground accounts for them coherently, and objections concerning inferential gaps and evil do not sever the cumulative inference.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory requirements of reality to a transcendent, intelligent, moral, and personal creator, thereby establishing theism as the fuller account.

centralBridges.description: Show that the universe's beginning, contingency, and order require a cause beyond space, time, and matter rather than an unexplained natural origin.
Show that rational inference, biological information, and the presuppositions of science require immaterial and intelligent foundations that material processes alone do not supply.
Show that objective duties, rights, and judgments of good and evil require an authoritative standard beyond individuals and changing societies.
Reconcile divine power and goodness with suffering through freedom, the distinction between knowledge and causation, epistemic limits, and the possibility of wider goods or justice.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish causal and design inferences drawn from asserted positive features from an appeal that merely inserts God wherever present knowledge is incomplete.
Connect human agency and the stable operation of natural laws to a sustaining personal ground rather than exclusively determined molecular activity.

routes.description: Establish that disciplined natural inquiry, provisional uncertainty, evolutionary and social explanations, and direct human responsibility account for the relevant evidence without positing an unverified supernatural being, while testing the internal coherence of the proposed theistic explanation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if natural and human-centered accounts remain adequate to the disputed phenomena, supernatural conclusions exceed the available evidential warrant, and the proposed divine attributes create unresolved explanatory problems rather than supplying a necessary ground.

motionBridge.description: Connect evidential restraint, natural explanation, and human ownership of moral choice to atheism's claimed superiority as an account of reality.

centralBridges.description: Show that conclusions about supernatural origins go beyond verified evidence and that acknowledged uncertainty is preferable to filling unresolved questions with divine agency.
Explain apparent cosmic and biological design through observer selection, local habitability, gradual evolution, and natural processes without inferring intentional arrangement.
Ground moral judgment, empathy, and responsibility in social decision-making and evolved cooperative capacities without requiring an objective divine lawgiver.
Show that apparently needless suffering, divine foreknowledge, and divine control of initial conditions challenge the joint claims of omnipotence, omniscience, and benevolence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require theism to explain how a law-transcending cause operates and why assigning divine attributes adds explanatory content rather than relocating unanswered questions.
Test whether religious chronology and interpretive claims independently predict discoveries or are revised after natural inquiry establishes contrary evidence.

sections.title: Cosmic origin, fine-tuning, and supernatural inference
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal clash over whether the universe's beginning and apparent calibration warrant a transcendent cause or instead require evidential restraint, observer-selection analysis, and continued natural inquiry.

sections.title: Reason, biological information, evolution, and science
sections.rationale: This issue tests competing accounts of rational reliability, DNA information, apparent biological design, and the conceptual foundations of scientific inquiry, all of which bear directly on each worldview's explanatory reach.

sections.title: Moral standards, empathy, and human responsibility
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether moral obligation requires a transcendent objective standard or can arise through social judgment, evolved empathy, and human ownership of choices, making it central to both stated burdens.

sections.title: Evil, suffering, freedom, and divine attributes
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether evil supports an objective moral ground, can be reconciled with a good and powerful creator, or instead renders the proposed divine attributes internally difficult to sustain.

sections.title: Comparative explanation, falsifiability, and epistemic method
sections.rationale: This issue integrates the motion-level dispute over positive inference, gaps reasoning, falsifiability, honest uncertainty, religious adaptation, and what each side must provide for its account to qualify as the better explanation.
